question:
(a) Prove that $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{13}\right)-\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{33}{65}\right)$ by checking the principal-value interval of the difference.

(b) Hence evaluate $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{13}\right)-\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{33}{65}\right)$.
explanation:
(a)
Let
$$A=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{13}\right),\qquad B=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)$$
Both $A$ and $B$ are acute principal angles. Therefore,
$$\sin A=\frac{12}{13},\quad\cos A=\frac{5}{13}$$
and
$$\sin B=\frac{3}{5},\quad\cos B=\frac{4}{5}$$
Since $\dfrac{12}{13}>\dfrac{3}{5}$ and $\sin^{-1}x$ is increasing, $A>B$. Hence, $A-B$ is a positive acute angle.
Using the sine-difference formula,
$$\sin(A-B)=\sin A\cos B-\cos A\sin B$$
$$=\frac{12}{13}\cdot\frac{4}{5}-\frac{5}{13}\cdot\frac{3}{5}$$
$$=\frac{48}{65}-\frac{15}{65}=\frac{33}{65}$$
Since $A-B\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, it lies in the principal range of $\sin^{-1}$. Therefore,
$$A-B=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{33}{65}\right)$$

(b)
Using the result from part (a), the expression becomes
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{33}{65}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{33}{65}\right)$$
Applying
$$\sin^{-1}t+\cos^{-1}t=\frac{\pi}{2}$$
gives
$$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{12}{13}\right)-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)+\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{33}{65}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}$$
Hence, the required value is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

options.D:
